That said , the main way it's going to bite us in the ass is the sudden massive influx of additional "money" into the system.

The more money you have in circulation relative to things of actual value, the less each piece of money can purchase - inflation. With a sudden, large increase in the amount of money in circulation, there's a risk that you'll see a sudden and large decrease in how much each piece of money that you already had before hand is worth. In other words, a sudden jump in prices without any increase in your income.

If the US dollar does weaken due to inflation and become able to purchase less, the government will need more dollars to keep doing the things that it wants to do… And where will it get them? Then, the US government will just have to print the dollars… Which is almost always guaranteed recipe for more inflation, especially if the reason that you're printing dollars in first place is to give yourself more purchasing power because of inflation.

TL;DR prices will rise, income will not.

P.S. historically, Other countries with less stable economies or less scrupulous financial institutions have used the United States dollar as their "reserve currency" to protect themselves from other countries doing this sort of crap, because this sort of thing hasn't really happened in the US ever, and pretty much every country in the world trusts the US dollar to keep behaving that way.
